headline: Broad sales gains and tariff refunds lift profit, outlook up
summary_short: Net sales of $27,067M grew 7.1% y/y with comparable sales +5.6%; diluted EPS of $2.65 compares with $1.51 a year ago, including $0.50 of tariff refund benefit.
summary_long: Comparable traffic rose 5.0% and digital comparable sales rose 9.8%. Gross margin rate expanded 2.3 points, 1.1 of which came from $301M of tariff refunds. SG&A rate was 21.9%. Full-year guidance now sees net sales growth around 6%, operating margin around 6.2%, and EPS of $10.65 to $11.40 including about $2.14 of tariff refunds. 2027 capex is expected at $5B to $6B. Cash was $4,464M; $251M of shares were repurchased in the quarter.
confidence_notes: Figures are taken from the press release. The shard's Yahoo-sourced diluted EPS ($4.11) and net income ($1,877M) do not match the release and were not used. Tariff refunds contributed $301M pretax to gross margin and operating income.

drivers.explanation: Merchandise sales rose 6.9% and non-merchandise sales rose 19.3%, helped by Roundel ad revenue, Circle Card profit sharing, Circle 360 membership and the Target+ marketplace.
Comparable traffic grew 5.0%; store comparable sales grew 4.6% and digital grew 9.8%.

Tariff refunds added 1.1 points. Excluding them, margin expanded about 1.2 points on lapping elevated markdowns and tariffs, non-merchandise growth and supply chain productivity, partly offset by freight, fuel and value investments.
Includes a $301M tariff refund benefit; SG&A rate was flat y/y at 21.9% as higher incentive pay and store labor offset sales leverage.
Management cites momentum from strategic investments and expects November sales in line with its guidance, accelerating from October.
